provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)

issues.text: The report argues the paper needs a much more robust discussion of the ethics of the experiments, including engagement with the literature on experimental ethics and election interference, and justification of the interventions. Purely informational treatments are not sufficient justification, since the content could be seen as propaganda by others.
issues.quote: I think a more robust discussion of the studies' ethics is warranted. There is an extensive literature in both political science and economics that focuses on the ethics of experiments, in particular regarding election interference.

issues.text: The evaluator questions the use of post-treatment values as outcomes in both experiments, arguing this is problematic given the imbalance and ex ante differences between control and treatment groups.
issues.quote: Both experiments use as their outcome variables the post-treatment observations: beliefs or voting intentions in the online experiment and vote shares in the field experiment.

issues.text: Ex ante differences in the outcome variables between control and treatment groups are a concern, and the paper's own note that effects shrink when pre-treatment values are controlled for heightens this worry. Controlling for pre-treatment values is included in the field experiment but not the online experiment.
issues.quote: I am concerned about the ex ante differences in the outcome variables between the control and the treatment groups. This concern is exacerbated by what the authors write on page 19

issues.text: The paper should use the difference between post- and pre-treatment outcomes rather than post-treatment levels; the evaluator notes this is straightforward for the online experiment but sees no obvious way for the field experiment.
issues.quote: Even better, why don't the authors use the difference between post- and pre-treatment values instead of only the post-treatment values. This would be straightforward for the online experiment

issues.text: The authors should calculate persuasion rates of the treatment (DellaVigna and Kaplan, 2007), which would help compare the findings with other contexts and interventions.
issues.quote: I would like the authors to calculate, if possible, the persuasion rates of their treatment (DellaVigna and Kaplan, 2007)

issues.text: The term 'reached tertiary education' is unclear; it is not specified whether it means any post-completion or another threshold.
issues.quote: I don't know what "reached tertiary education" (p. 17) means. Please clarify whether this refers to any post-completion, or another threshold.
